verdict: Broadcom's revenue jumped 47% to $13.1B as VMware transformed its software business — but a one-time $4.5B non-cash tax charge on an internal IP transfer turned a solid operating profit into a $1.9B net loss on paper.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: a loss — driven by the one-time tax charge; non-GAAP EPS was $1.24

kpis.label: Infrastructure software revenue
kpis.note: +200% YoY with VMware in the fold

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. Broadcom expected AI revenue to reach $12B for fiscal 2024 as a whole.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — nearly tripled YoY with a full quarter of VMware included (the deal closed in November 2023).

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring and other charges.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,064M on Broadcom's debt, plus $82M of other income, less a $443M loss from discontinued operations — a net -$1,425M below operating profit.
footerNote: Net loss of $1,875M includes the $443M loss from discontinued operations, folded into the chart's 'Other expense' step; continuing operations lost $1,432M after the one-time tax provision. Per-share figures are as reported in the release, which restated them for Broadcom's ten-for-one stock split.

takeaways.title: VMware remade the mix
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue nearly tripled to $5.8B with a full quarter of VMware included — software was 44% of Broadcom's revenue, up from 22% a year ago.

takeaways.title: A paper tax charge flipped the quarter to a loss
takeaways.text: Moving IP rights into the U.S. as part of a supply-chain realignment triggered a one-time, non-cash tax provision of about $4.5B. The business itself earned $3.8B of operating income, and on Broadcom's non-GAAP view net income was $6,120M.

takeaways.title: Cash kept pouring in
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $4.8B — 37% of revenue — and adjusted EBITDA reached $8.2B, 63% of revenue, even as the GAAP bottom line showed a loss.

oneTimers: One-time tax provision: about $4.5B, non-cash — a discrete charge from an intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States as part of a supply-chain realignment. It is the whole reason the quarter shows a GAAP net loss.

GAAP profit carries $2,337M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,525M inside cost of revenue and $812M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $6,120M instead of a $1,875M loss.
Discontinued operations lost $443M below the line — businesses being exited; the loss from continuing operations was $1,432M.
